title: Components
description: Primitives the design system does not have yet.

paragraphs:
Components
11 November 2026

/styles lists fourteen Edit primitives. They cover choosing, typing and confirming. They do not yet cover continuous values, finding a command, hearing back from the system, or doing something dangerous on purpose.
Each of these would be added the way the conventions ask: built once, listed on /styles, mirrored in Figma, then used.
#134 asks for a shared slider. Three shapes cover what the panels need.

A plain slider for a continuous value. A slider with detents for the spacing scale, where notches cut into the track show the stops so they need no labels. And a scrub field for numbers that come in sets, such as a crop rectangle: drag the axis letter sideways to change the number, hold Shift for bigger steps, or type.
All three use native inputs. Both sliders put the label and current value inside a compact row, with the fill showing the position behind them.
Drag the sliders. Drag the X, Y, W or H letter sideways; arrow keys work in the field.
Edit is driven by shortcuts and by knowing where things are. The Shortcuts panel lists them, but you have to know to open it. For one author that is fine. For anyone else it is the first wall.

A command menu makes every action findable by typing its name, and shows the shortcut beside it, so using the menu teaches the shortcut. It is the Menu component with a search field on top and group headings in the status type. It needs one new atom, a keycap, which the Shortcuts panel would then share.
It is also where Insert belongs when the page is long and the insert bar is off screen.
Type “pub” or “image”. Arrow keys move, Enter runs, Esc clears.

When Save finishes, the bar’s status text changes and that is all. When a block is deleted, it is gone and Cmd+Z is the only way back, if it works for that edit. There is no place for the system to say what just happened.

A toast is that place, and for destructive actions it carries the way back. Three rules keep it calm: one line and at most one action; newer toasts sit in front and older ones step back; pointing at the stack fans it out and holds the timers. It is built on the same surface as the save bar, so it looks like it belongs beside it.
Press all three, then hover the stack.
Delete project is a Danger button. Pressing it has to be followed by some confirmation, and a dialog asking “are you sure?” is the pattern everyone clicks through.

Holding is a confirmation that cannot be clicked through by habit. The button fills while it is held and acts when the fill arrives; letting go early rewinds it faster than it filled. It works with the pointer, with touch, and with Space or Enter held on the keyboard. Paired with a toast that offers Undo, a destructive action is both deliberate and recoverable.
Press and hold. Let go halfway once to see it rewind.
Keycap. Introduced by the command menu. A 20px key with a one-pixel bottom edge, in the badge’s ink.

Bar. The save bar, format bar, gap pill and insert bar are four hand-built versions of one floating surface: 12px radius, 6px padding, 6px gap. Naming it would let the save bar use Button directly and remove its private button styles.
Sheet. The container half of the phone proposal in the panels report.
Progress. Uploads and Publish take seconds and show a spinner. A determinate hairline along the bar’s bottom edge would say how long.

The slider, since it is already requested and unblocks the inherited-values pattern. Then Bar, which is a refactor with no new design and removes a known source of drift. Toast and hold-to-confirm should arrive together.
